key_insight: Strain controls iodine-vacancy pair dynamics in CsPbI3: strong isotropic compression favors separation, tension promotes pair-preserving relay hopping, and biaxial compression produces orientation-dependent behavior.
engineering_relevance: Strain and vacancy-pair orientation may offer design variables for managing defect migration and structural stability in halide perovskites.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies under isotropic and biaxial strain.
Analysis of short-time hopping, pair separation, and relay motion.
Static vacancy-interaction calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential.
evidence_signal: MLMD shows nonmonotonic strain-dependent hopping fractions, while DFT and SevenNet-0 yield repulsive vacancy interactions for every configuration examined.
watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior does not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device-scale reliability.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
